details.intro:
The Euangelium Euae (Gospel of Eve) was a Gnostic revelation text known solely through an extensive quotation preserved by Epiphanius of Salamis in his Panarion (Haer. 26.2–3, 5), directed against the "Gnostics" or Borborites / Phibionites.

The preserved fragment is an ecstatic hymn of pantheistic / panentheistic cosmic revelation: "I stood upon a lofty mountain and saw a huge man, and another of diminished stature; and I heard as it were a voice of thunder, and drew near to hear; and he spoke to me and said: 'I am thou, and thou art I, and wherever thou art, there am I; and in all things am I dispersed...'"
details.provenance:
Language: Greek.
Date: 2nd–3rd century CE; Roman Egypt / Syria.
Attestation: Epiphanius of Salamis, Panarion (Adversus Haereses) 26.2.6 (ed. Holl, GCS 25, 1915, pp. 278–280).
details.manuscripts:
• Sole Direct Witness: Epiphanius, Panarion 26.2.6 (preserved in MSS Vaticanus gr. 503, Venetus Marcianus gr. 44).
  • Indirect Mention: Resch, Agrapha, apocryphon 52.
